form.label: Kong Proxy - Upstream and Balancer Health
form.description: Per-target pod health behind vault-svc and admin-api. Answers "which backend is sick" and "did a pod silently leave the pool". Balancer retries are the early warning that precedes user-visible 5xx.

search.query: `kong_topology_source` | stats count by service | sort service
`kong_proxied` | search $svc$ | where isnotnull(upstream_ip) | stats dc(upstream_ip) as targets
`kong_base` | search $svc$ | stats count as total, sum(retried) as r | eval pct=if(total>0, round(r*100/total,3), 0) | fields pct

html.p: max_retries is read per-service from service.retries in the log, not assumed - so this is each service's own configured budget. A request whose try_count exceeds it has exhausted its retries: Kong ran out of targets to try and the failure reached the user. Retries otherwise hide an unhealthy backend completely - users see 200s and the error rate stays flat - so exhaustion is the moment that stops being true.

search.query: `kong_base` | search $svc$ | stats count as requests, values(max_retries) as configured_retries, max(try_count) as most_attempts_seen, sum(retried) as retried_requests, sum(retries_exhausted) as exhausted_requests, sum(eval(if(retries_exhausted==1 AND status>=500,1,0))) as exhausted_and_failed by service, upstream_host | eval retry_pct = round(retried_requests*100/requests, 3), budget_used_pct = round(most_attempts_seen*100/(configured_retries+1), 0) | fields service, upstream_host, requests, configured_retries, most_attempts_seen, budget_used_pct, retried_requests, retry_pct, exhausted_requests, exhausted_and_failed | sort - exhausted_requests, - retry_pct

html.p: A step change here is a pool membership change. Down = a pod was scaled down, failed a readiness probe, or crashed. Up = a scale-out. A flat line at 1 means every request depends on a single pod.

search.query: `kong_proxied` | search $svc$ | where isnotnull(upstream_ip) | timechart span=$span$ dc(upstream_ip) as targets by service

html.p: upstream_ip is the LAST entry in the tries array - the target that ultimately served the request. mins_since_last flags a pod that has stopped receiving traffic entirely.

search.query: `kong_proxied` | search $svc$ | where isnotnull(upstream_ip) | stats count as requests, sum(eval(if(status>=500,1,0))) as c5xx, sum(eval(if(status>=400,1,0))) as errors, p50(proxy_ms) as p50_ms, p95(proxy_ms) as p95_ms, max(proxy_ms) as max_ms, max(_time) as last_seen by service, upstream_ip | eventstats sum(requests) as fleet_total by service | eval share_pct = round(requests*100/fleet_total, 1), error_pct = round(errors*100/requests, 2), p50_ms = round(p50_ms,0), p95_ms = round(p95_ms,0), max_ms = round(max_ms,0), mins_since_last= round((now()-last_seen)/60, 1) | fields service, upstream_ip, requests, share_pct, error_pct, c5xx, p50_ms, p95_ms, max_ms, mins_since_last | sort service, - requests
`kong_proxied` | search $svc$ | where isnotnull(upstream_ip) | timechart span=$span$ p95(proxy_ms) by upstream_ip
`kong_base` | search $svc$ | timechart span=$span$ sum(retried) as retried, count as requests | eval retry_pct=if(requests>0, round(retried*100/requests,3), 0) | fields _time, retried, retry_pct

panel.title: Which target is causing the retries?

html.p: For a retried request, the FIRST entry in tries is the attempt that failed and the LAST is the one that succeeded. A pod appearing repeatedly as failed_first_try while rarely appearing as upstream_ip is the unhealthy one - and Kong is masking it from users by retrying, so it will not show up in the 5xx rate until it gets worse.

search.query: `kong_base` | search $svc$ | where retried==1 | eval failed_first_try=mvindex('tries{}.ip', 0) | stats count as retry_events, values(status) as resulting_status, max(try_count) as max_tries by service, failed_first_try | sort - retry_events | head 25

html.p: Time for Kong to pick a target, from tries[].balancer_latency_ns, shown in microseconds because the millisecond field rounds to 0 on a healthy system. A sustained rise points at DNS or service-discovery trouble, not at the upstream itself.

search.query: `kong_base` | search $svc$ | eval balancer_us = tonumber(mvindex('tries{}.balancer_latency_ns', -1)) / 1000 | where isnotnull(balancer_us) | timechart span=$span$ p50(balancer_us) as p50_us, p95(balancer_us) as p95_us, max(balancer_us) as max_us
